It is imposaibla. he save, to put a foot down on the paths when the sun is not wdhout Ire:ding upon some. They appear to have destroyed every Wade of gra,s, and are now climbing the trees bv hundreds. There is one piece of quite a hundred acres with not a green blade to he seen on it, and in other parts of the park similar patches of half an acre to 50 acres, and they are still spreading. Cattle shun the places as if they were poisonous. The caterpillars I. not appear to eat anything but grass, as weed..., kin, growing among it are untouched. There is o scarcity of small birds here, which may partly account (mooch a pest. What few rooks there are are dniag good work among the caterpillars, and the starlings feed on thon.
